messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Metformin is prescribed to manage polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
Metformin improves how the body responds to insulin.
PCOS affects about 1 in 10 women of reproductive age.
PCOS is often marked by insulin resistance.
In insulin resistance, the body doesn't respond well to insulin.
This lack of response prompts the pancreas to produce more insulin.
This excess insulin drives up androgen production.
Androgen is a male hormone.
This process worsens symptoms like irregular periods, infertility, acne, and excess hair growth.
Metformin helps by lowering insulin levels.
Metformin helps by decreasing the liver's glucose production.
Metformin helps by improving glucose uptake by muscles.
Metformin helps by reducing circulating androgen levels.
Reducing circulating androgen levels can support more regular ovulation.
Reducing circulating androgen levels can support more regular menstrual cycles.
Metformin is not FDA-approved to treat PCOS.
Metformin is widely prescribed as an off-label treatment.
Metformin is prescribed particularly for those with insulin resistance.
Triples: [["Metformin", "treats", "polycystic ovary syndrome"], ["Metformin", "improves", "insulin response"], ["PCOS", "affects", "1 in 10 women of reproductive age"], ["PCOS", "marked by", "insulin resistance"], ["insulin resistance", "defined by", "poor insulin response"], ["insulin resistance", "causes", "increased insulin production"], ["increased insulin production", "leads to", "increased androgen production"], ["androgen", "is a", "male hormone"], ["increased androgen production", "worsens", "irregular periods"], ["increased androgen production", "worsens", "infertility"], ["increased androgen production", "worsens", "acne"], ["increased androgen production", "worsens", "excess hair growth"], ["Metformin", "reduces", "insulin levels"], ["Metformin", "reduces", "liver glucose production"], ["Metformin", "improves", "muscle glucose uptake"], ["Metformin", "reduces", "circulating androgen levels"], ["reduced circulating androgen levels", "supports", "regular ovulation"], ["reduced circulating androgen levels", "supports", "regular menstrual cycles"], ["Metformin", "not fda approved for", "PCOS"], ["Metformin", "used off label for", "PCOS"], ["Metformin", "prescribed for", "insulin resistance"]]
Relations: ["affects", "causes", "defined by", "improves", "is a", "leads to", "marked by", "not fda approved for", "prescribed for", "reduces", "supports", "treats", "used off label for", "worsens"]
Answer:

completion:
affects: The subject condition or entity impacts or influences the specified population or entity.
causes: The subject condition or process leads to or results in the specified effect or outcome.
defined by: The subject condition is characterized or defined by the specified feature or characteristic.
improves: The subject drug or intervention enhances or positively affects the specified physiological process or condition.
is a: The subject entity is classified as or is an example of the specified category or type.
leads to: The subject condition or process results in or contributes to the specified effect or outcome.
marked by: The subject condition is commonly associated with or characterized by the specified symptom or feature.
not fda approved for: The subject drug is not officially approved by the FDA for the specified medical condition or use.
prescribed for: The subject drug is medically prescribed or recommended for the specified condition or purpose.
reduces: The subject drug or intervention decreases or lowers the specified physiological parameter or condition.
supports: The subject intervention or condition facilitates or contributes to the specified physiological process or outcome.
treats: The subject drug is used to manage or address the specified medical condition.
used off label for: The subject drug is prescribed for a medical condition or use that is not officially approved by regulatory authorities.
worsens: The subject condition or process exacerbates or aggravates the specified symptom or condition.
